diagnosis: Either: Counts the starting number as the first count rather than counting the jumps back. Or: Counts back only 2 instead of 3.
rationale: The learner said '12, 11, 10' for 12 - 3, including 12 in the 3 counts and landing on 10 instead of making 3 hops back to 9. A number line demonstration of subtracting by hops makes it visible that the first hop lands on the number before the start.

script.focus: Notice that the first hop lands on the number before the start.

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,4]. Tutor points at: Notice that the first hop lands on the number before the start.

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration directly addresses the exact misconception ('Start at 14. We have not hopped yet', 'Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started'). It uses a worked demo representation (passive visual sequence rather than interactive student plotting), simplifies the cognitive load, stays well within Grade 1 scope, and uses a different problem (14 - 4 instead of 12 - 3) so it does not leak the answer.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this worked demo directly models and explains the concept of hopping before counting.
